name: Halide
tagline: A manual camera app for iPhone with RAW capture, real exposure controls, and its own image processing pipeline.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Halide has historically sold both a subscription and a lifetime unlock, so the monthly figure is not a clean number.

verdictSummary: The boring truth is that most of Halide's manual controls are public AVFoundation surface: ISO, shutter duration, focus distance, white balance, bayer RAW capture to DNG. An agent that knows SwiftUI can hand you a working manual camera with a histogram, focus peaking, and a RAW writer in a weekend, and it will genuinely be fun to use. What it cannot hand you is Process Zero, the neural macro and upscaling work, or the years of per sensor tuning across every iPhone Apple has shipped. You also inherit the Apple tax: a Mac, Xcode, and a developer account if you want the thing to live on your phone longer than a week. So it is buildable, but you are building a nice toy camera next to a very carefully tuned instrument.
coreLoopDIY: A SwiftUI iOS camera app with manual ISO, shutter, focus and white balance, live histogram and focus peaking, and RAW DNG plus JPEG capture straight into your photo library.
requirements: A Mac with a recent Xcode
An iPhone running a current iOS, since the simulator has no camera
An Apple Developer account if you want the build to survive past the 7 day free provisioning window
Comfort reading AVFoundation docs when the agent guesses wrong about capture device formats
whatYouLose: Process Zero and the rest of Halide's own demosaic and tone pipeline, which is the actual reason people talk about the app
Neural macro, telephoto upscaling and the other ML assisted capture modes
Per device tuning across a decade of iPhone sensors, so your RAWs will look flat and your JPEGs worse than the stock camera
Interface craft: one handed gestures, haptics, the loupe, all the things that make a manual camera usable while a moment is happening
Someone else fixing your camera app the week iOS ships a breaking change
moatNotes: The API surface is public. The taste applied on top of it is not, and neither is the willingness to re-tune for every new sensor Apple ships.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a camera app is judged in the half second between seeing something and capturing it, and that is exactly where a weekend build falls apart. Halide is paid for by people who already own a free camera app that is objectively better at computational photography, and who want manual control plus a specific look plus an interface that does not make them think. A one-shot build gets you the manual control. The look and the reflexes are the product.
notes: Rare case where the SaaS moat is not data or network, just craft and a lot of sensor specific patience.
prompt:
Build a manual camera app for iPhone in an empty folder. Stack: Swift, SwiftUI, AVFoundation. No third party packages. No accounts, no analytics, no cloud, no telemetry.

Target iOS 17 and up. Portrait orientation only for v1.

Core:
- Full screen live preview using AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer wrapped in a UIViewRepresentable.
- Camera picker for the available back cameras plus the front camera, using AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession. Handle devices that do not have a telephoto.
- Manual controls as horizontal sliders that appear one at a time: ISO, shutter duration, focus distance, white balance in kelvin. Each slider clamps to the active device format's real min and max, read at runtime, not hardcoded.
- An AUTO toggle per control that returns that parameter to continuous auto mode.
- Capture button writes both a bayer RAW DNG and a JPEG using AVCapturePhotoOutput with a RAW plus processed settings pair. Skip RAW gracefully if the current device or format does not support it.
- Save to the user's photo library via PHPhotoLibrary, RAW and JPEG as one asset with two resources. Request permission properly.

Viewfinder aids:
- Live luminance histogram drawn in a Canvas, fed from AVCaptureVideoDataOutput frames, downsampled hard so it does not tank the frame rate.
- Focus peaking overlay: a cheap edge detect on the video frames, tinted overlay on in focus edges, toggleable.
- A readout row showing current ISO, shutter, and whether values are locked or auto.

Explicitly out of scope: video recording, any custom RAW demosaic or tone mapping, portrait or depth modes, editing, sharing sheets, an iPad layout, a settings screen.

Write it as a normal Xcode project structure with an .xcodeproj I can open. Put the required camera and photo library usage strings in Info.plist. If a value must be configurable, use a .env style Config.swift with comments, but this app should need no secrets. Add a README with the exact steps to run it on a real device including the free provisioning caveat, and a short section listing what will look worse than the stock camera and why.
